subject: GCP Marketplace usage cutoff & EFT collection plan
messages:
From: Alice Hsu <alice.hsu@gigacloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T15:22:00Z
Subject: GCP marketplace usage mismatch / invoice shortfall (May)

Hi Marissa,

We ran a reconciliation between our metering and the GCP Marketplace invoice Redwood sent for May. Marketplace metering shows ~22% more SKUs billed for two of our listings compared to the usage export we receive directly from GCP. That explains the $32,450 shortfall on the May invoice.

Key asks: can you confirm what your marketplace cutoff/timezone is for counting usage (UTC vs PST)? Also we need EFT instructions to initiate the pending payment (we can wire once we confirm the final invoice).

I've attached our metered extract and the Redwood invoice PDF from our portal for reference.

Attachments:
- GigaCloud_metered_usage_export_202805.csv (CSV, ~1.1MB)
- GigaCloud_May_Invoice_202805.pdf (PDF, ~220KB)

Thanks,
Alice
Billing Operations
GigaCloud
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Hsu <alice.hsu@gigacloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: GCP marketplace usage mismatch / invoice shortfall (May)

Alice — thanks for the heads up and for sending the extract. I'm looping in Ben (finance) and Karthik (accounts) to help reconcile and confirm cutoff windows.

Quick answers up front: Redwood aligns marketplace metering to GCP's metering window which is UTC-based and uses a 00:00-23:59 UTC day by default, but some listings can be recorded with a small delay depending on how GCP reports usage. We'll need to compare your CSV rows (timestamps) against our portal logs to identify double-counted listing events.

Action plan (we'll own this):
- Ben / Finance to run a match between your CSV and our marketplace billing events and surface any duplicate listing IDs. Target: initial findings by EOD tomorrow.
- If we confirm an over-bill on Redwood's invoice, we'll issue a credit/memo and propose netting on the next invoice OR apply an immediate refund — whichever you prefer.
- I'll send our EFT instructions (PDF) so you can prepare the wire.

Attaching: Redwood_EFT_instructions.pdf (bank details + remittance template). Also linking the HubSpot deal so we keep procurement in sync: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/4821

Appreciate the quick follow-up — we'll move fast.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partner Billing, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_EFT_instructions.pdf]
From: Alice Hsu <alice.hsu@gigacloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOne <procureone@procureone.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: GCP marketplace usage mismatch / invoice shortfall (May)

Marissa — thanks. A couple of clarifications from our side after a quick look:
- The two listings in question (gc-standard and gc-ops-agent) were migrated on 2028-05-03; during the migration window both the old and new listing IDs were active for ~18 hours which likely caused duplicated metering records at GCP's side.
- Our CSV timestamps are in PST and show spikes between 07:00-09:00 PST on 2028-05-03 (which is 14:00-16:00 UTC). If Redwood's aggregation uses a strict UTC day boundary that shouldn't double-count, but if Redwood ingests both the old and new listing IDs as separate SKUs into the invoice generator that would.

I've re-sent the CSV with the raw row IDs and a small mapping file to show the two listing IDs side-by-side.

Attachments:
- GigaCloud_metered_usage_export_202805.csv (updated)
- listing-id-mapping.csv

ProcureOne — can you confirm how you'll be wiring for the May invoice once the corrected amount is confirmed? We prefer a netted adjustment on the July invoice rather than two separate transfers.

Regards,
Alice
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Hsu <alice.hsu@gigacloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: GCP marketplace usage mismatch / invoice shortfall (May)

Thanks, Alice & Marissa. We dug into the ledger and here's what we found (high level):

- Root cause: duplicate listing ingestion on Redwood's side during the migration window. The ingestion pipeline created two usage records (old/new listing IDs) for ~18 hours on 2028-05-03. That produced about $30,900 in duplicated billable units after our model weighting.
- Cutoff asymmetry: GCP reports at the listing level but some of our downstream aggregation deduplicated by product name only; because the old/new IDs had identical product names, the dedupe failed until we matched listing_id.

Proposed remediation (please confirm preference):
1) Issue a credit memo for $30,900 and apply it as a netting adjustment against the July invoice (preferred for AP efficiency).
2) Alternatively, we can process an immediate refund by wire — we can expedite if you need cashflow sooner.

Tax/VAT note: the credit will need to carry a VAT reason code in the credit memo. Alice, can you confirm your billing entity (VAT ID) so we create the credit with the right tax attributes?

I've attached a draft ledger adjustment for your review: ledger-adjustment-draft.xlsx (shows GL impact and reclassification). We'll hold action until we have your sign-off.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ledger-adjustment-draft.xlsx]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: GCP marketplace usage mismatch / invoice shortfall (May)

Hi Alice — thanks for confirming the listing migration window and for the updated CSV.

We are aligned on the netting approach: Redwood prefers to net the $30,900 credit against July's invoice to keep the cadence simple for both teams. If that works for ProcureOne, we'll produce a credit memo with the VAT reason code and include the payment instructions for the netted amount.

For speed, I've created an amendment (DocuSign) that authorizes applying the credit to the next invoice. Please sign here: https://www.docusign.net/AMR-3245234

If you need a wire instead, let us know and we'll share Redwood's bank remittance details (we included a PDF earlier).

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
